# Purpose
This document explains and demonstrates `sales_analysis.R`, which summarizes fictional retail sales using base R.

## Inputs
The input file is `synthetic_sales.csv`, with columns `date`, `category`, `quantity`, and `unit_price`. All records are synthetic.

## Method
Revenue is calculated per record as quantity multiplied by unit price, then summed by category.

```{r load-data}
sales <- read.csv("synthetic_sales.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(c("date", "category", "quantity", "unit_price") %in% names(sales)))
head(sales)
```

```{r calculate-revenue}
sales$revenue <- sales$quantity * sales$unit_price
category_totals <- aggregate(revenue ~ category, data = sales, FUN = sum)
category_totals <- category_totals[order(category_totals$category), ]
category_totals
```

## Outputs
The output includes a category revenue table and the following chart.

```{r chart, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
barplot(category_totals$revenue, names.arg = category_totals$category,
        main = "Synthetic Revenue by Category", ylab = "Revenue (CAD)",
        col = "steelblue")
```

## Verification
Before submission, run the script independently and knit this document. Compare the category totals with manual calculations and note the actual results in `Appendix.md`.

## Limitations
These records are invented for education and do not represent real retail transactions.
